observations: Photo 0: one flat panel TV leaning against a wall on a tiled floor, front view at an angle.
Photo 0: thin silver or grey metal bezel on all four sides, glossy black screen.
Photo 0: the screen is off and reflects the room; no picture is shown.
Photo 0: no logo, badge or text is readable on the bezel or anywhere in the frame.
Photo 0: no stand, feet, remote or power cable visible.
Photo 0: no crack or chip visible on the screen glass from this angle; the back and the label are not shown.
Photo 0: compared with the floor tiles the panel looks large, roughly in the 50 to 55 inch class, but the size cannot be measured.

identity.kind: flat screen smart TV, about 55 inch

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a large panel but no size label; the back label or a tape measure across the diagonal is missing.
No Samsung logo or label is visible in photo 0.
The screen is off; no home screen or apps are shown.

risks.risk: Brand, model and year unknown, which set the price of a TV.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the label on the back showing brand, model number and size.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced; the label shot is needed

risks.risk: TV does not power on, or the panel has lines, dead pixels, dark patches or backlight failure.
risks.proof: Clip of the TV switched on from the wall socket, showing a full bright white and a moving picture across the whole screen.

risks.risk: Not actually a smart TV, or the smart functions fail.
risks.proof: Clip of the home screen opening an app such as YouTube.
Photo of the stand legs and the remote with the TV.

risks.risk: Back casing or ports damaged, or the TV has been opened for repair.
risks.proof: Photo of the whole back and the ports.

proof_requests: Photo of the back label showing brand, model number and size.
Clip of the TV powered on, showing a full white screen and then the smart home screen opening an app.
Photo of the whole back with the ports.
Photo of the stand and remote, if included.
response.reason: The photo shows a large flat screen TV that is switched off, with no readable brand, model or size, and those set the price of a TV; the back label shot is needed before even a worst case price can be set.
